Manuscript.detail: 10 numbered statements, 10 byte-identical Appendix B modules, and all 17 theorem links in Table 3.

Baseline.detail: 46 of 46 checks in seven original programs.

Numerical data.detail: Compared all six freshly generated CSVs with the released data.

Coverage.detail: 21 distinct rows cover the release inventory, supplemental results and open inputs.

Regression controls.detail: Six controls exercised altered claims, embedded proof text, printed coefficients, axiom records and open-input classifications.

Lean.detail: Fresh Lean 4.36.0 processes accepted all 17 frozen proofs, all 20 supporting proofs and 6 supplemental proofs. The six returned modules and isolated final packet also passed.

claims.title: Time-unit and gap-ratio scaling
claims.scope: Symmetric finite-dimensional operators and positive time units.
claims.observed: Exact coefficient and gap-ratio identities; three positive scalings of a degenerate ground space.

claims.label: Theorem 2.1
claims.title: Matching errors for two calibrations
claims.scope: Physical identification of F requires speed preservation and time covariance.
claims.observed: 108 admissible rational steps checked exactly, including zero and nonzero truncation residuals.

claims.label: Theorem 3.1
claims.title: Uniform endpoint limit
claims.scope: The physical interpretation assumes dispersion; uniformity uses a fixed regular clock and the stated running bounds.
claims.observed: Series through degree two and exact telescoping for 15 paths, including zero steps and perturbed decrements.

claims.label: Proposition 3.2
claims.title: Power-law drift of a linear multiplier
claims.scope: Exact one-loop sequence with positive denominators and b + κ > 0.
claims.observed: High-precision finite products and normalized large-length limits for negative, zero and positive drift.

claims.label: Corollary 3.3
claims.title: Physical drift coefficient
claims.scope: Follows by combining the physical ratio expansion with the drift criterion.
claims.observed: The physical ratio has zero linear coefficient; the compatibility obstruction at unit slope is exactly κ.

claims.label: Definition 4.1
claims.title: Clock on a centre-neutral excitation branch
claims.scope: Tests the gap expression and model group projectors. Identifying the physical glueball branch requires spectral input.
claims.observed: Exact gap-shift identity, cyclic momentum projectors for three sizes and all centre characters for N=2,3.

claims.label: Lemma 4.2
claims.title: Free axial speed and finite-size remainder
claims.scope: Prescribed free dispersion, L ≥ 2 and nonnegative rest mass.
claims.observed: 24 free-branch gap computations at 75 digits, including L=2 and L=100000; checked both signed inequalities.

claims.label: §4 interacting estimate
claims.title: Uniform interacting finite-volume hypothesis
claims.scope: Constants uniform in both L and g and the interacting branch identification remain open.
claims.observed: The free L²-scaled error stays bounded. A comparison sequence with error 1/L converges while its scaled error diverges. The interacting uniform bound is open.

claims.label: Proposition 5.1
claims.title: Unit speed of the retained free mode
claims.scope: Lean checks the alias separation inequality and the all-direction free phase bound. The two-time pole and overlap argument is analytic.
claims.observed: Exact alias identity and all eight aliases in 24 momentum/spacing cases; bounded the phase speed and recovered the late-time pole.

claims.label: §5 interacting speed
claims.title: One-loop dispersion hypothesis
claims.scope: Preservation of the selected interacting pole through one loop has no proof in this release.
claims.observed: Equal ground-state projectors coexist with different propagation speeds in a calculation with fixed time units. The interacting one-loop law remains open.

claims.label: §5 W2d.2
claims.title: Uniform small-field defect estimate
claims.scope: The model diagnoses the limitation of a one-sided comparison; a uniform gauge-theory estimate remains open.
claims.observed: A positive spectral shift satisfies the one-sided comparison in a model channel. Obtaining the W2d.2 uniform small-field estimate requires interacting input.

claims.label: §5 W2d.4
claims.title: Cancellation of the interacting order-g² loss
claims.scope: The algebraic cancellation assumes the two-mismatch ansatz. Completeness of that ansatz is open.
claims.observed: The proposed two-mismatch ansatz cancels its linear term. Its completeness for the interacting W2d.4 defect remains open.

claims.label: Proposition 6.1
claims.title: Group dependence of the Hamiltonian-limit kernel
claims.scope: Lean checks the group reduction after the moment identities. The input kernel and integral reductions are analytic inputs.
claims.observed: Reduced the Wilson kernel for general N; verified the two moment identities against the independent spatial moments at orders 20, 32 and 48.

claims.label: §6–7 numerical comparison
claims.title: Wilson coefficients and printed rounding
claims.scope: The two evaluations use the same kernel. The published-pair residuals exceed rounding for SU(2) and SU(3).
claims.observed: Both quadratures agree within 2×10⁻¹². Absolute printed-pair residuals: SU(2) 5.0148444e-05, SU(3) 6.2367011e-05. Both exceed 10⁻⁵.

claims.label: Proposition 8.1
claims.title: Optional shift from Wilson truncation
claims.scope: Exact differentiation given the coefficient conventions and the assumed expansions.
claims.observed: Differentiated both definitions at zero; matching their slopes gives (κE−κB)/2 = −Δc_irr.

claims.label: §8 Wilson shift values
claims.title: Group-specific Wilson truncation shifts
claims.scope: The numerical values of Δc_irr for SU(2) and SU(3) are undetermined by the coefficient identity.
claims.observed: Distinct choices satisfy the same identity. The optional group-specific shift is unevaluated in this paper.

claims.label: Proposition 8.2
claims.title: Passage from a direct remainder to its reciprocal
claims.scope: The supplement checks the quantified bound for every x in the interval, given the direct remainder and positive floor.
claims.observed: Exact numerator identity and 117 rational cases including zero, both signs and endpoints.

claims.label: §8 regularity
claims.title: Nonperturbative regularity on the weak interval
claims.scope: Positive C² regularity and a uniform remainder for the interacting clock remain open.
claims.observed: A normalized comparison clock with x² log(x) has the prescribed slope and an unbounded quadratic remainder. This tests the role of regularity.

claims.label: §8 strong endpoint
claims.title: Control of the strong-coupling endpoint clock
claims.scope: An independent strong-coupling value is required when the endpoint lies outside the weak interval.
claims.observed: Two positive extensions agree on the weak interval and through two derivatives at the cutoff, and yield different endpoint clocks. The strong endpoint needs independent data.

claims.label: §8 conditional transfer
claims.title: Conditional transfer and intermediate step count
claims.scope: Requires the stated per-step loss, running, propagation and endpoint inequalities.
claims.observed: Five saturated transfer chains and three exact threshold cases, including empty and overshooting segments.

claims.label: §7 / Appendix A
claims.title: Printed coefficient, step, product and free-box tables
claims.scope: The release theorem encloses A. Python validates the other displayed numerical values from newly generated data.
claims.observed: All 90 printed numeric results in Tables 1, 2, A1 and A2 match their fresh calculations at the displayed precision.
